name: Iced Latte
intro: An iced latte is espresso poured over cold milk and ice, giving you a cool, mellow drink that's creamy without being heavy. It's smooth and lightly sweet, with a coffee flavor that stays gentle. It's a go-to for warm days.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of an iced latte in a tall glass

vessel.name: Tall glass
vessel.note: Room for 1 cup of ice plus the liquids.

ingredients.note: From roughly 18 g of finely ground coffee.
Whole milk gives the creamiest result.

equipment.alternative: Moka pot or AeroPress (see home methods)

steps.title: Fill the glass
steps.body: Add 1 cup of ice to a tall glass. Starting with ice ready means the hot espresso is cooled quickly, which keeps flavors fresh and avoids a bitter, stewed taste.

steps.title: Pour in the milk
steps.body: Pour 6 oz of cold milk over the ice. Adding the milk before the espresso creates the classic layered look and helps cool things down.
steps.tip: Shake or stir the milk briefly if you add sweetener or syrup.

steps.title: Pull the espresso
steps.body: Pull a double shot of espresso, using about 18 g of finely ground coffee. Iced drinks dilute as the ice melts, so a strong, well-extracted shot is important.
steps.tip: If your iced lattes taste weak, try a slightly finer grind.

steps.title: Pour over
steps.body: Pour the hot espresso over the milk and ice. It will swirl into beautiful ribbons before blending.
steps.tip: Pour slowly if you want the layered look.

steps.title: Stir and sweeten
steps.body: Give it a gentle stir to blend. Taste and add sweetener now if you like, since sugar dissolves best while the shot is still warm.

steps.title: Serve right away
steps.body: Enjoy while the ice is fresh. Over time the ice melts and the flavor mellows.

homeMethods.note: Brew in a moka pot and pour over milk and ice. It tastes bold and slightly rustic, a nice stand-in, though it lacks the crema and smoothness of espresso.
A concentrated AeroPress shot over milk and ice is a clean, strong approximation. No crema, but the flavor works well when chilled.
Double-strength brewed coffee, cooled, with milk and ice makes an easy iced coffee. It will taste milder and thinner than a true iced latte. Making coffee ice cubes helps avoid watering it down.

tips: Larger ice cubes dilute your drink more slowly.
Coffee ice cubes are a great trick to keep flavor strong.
Dissolve sugar in the warm espresso or use simple syrup, as granulated sugar doesn't dissolve well in cold drinks.
commonMistakes: Using too little ice so the espresso melts it fast.
Making a weak shot that vanishes in cold milk.
Letting it sit and become watery.

variations.name: Vanilla iced latte
variations.description: Add 1 to 2 tsp of vanilla syrup to the glass before the milk.

variations.name: Oat milk iced latte
variations.description: Oat milk makes a creamy, slightly sweet iced latte. Results vary by brand.

variations.name: Iced mocha
variations.description: Stir chocolate syrup into the espresso before pouring over milk and ice.

seo.title: How to Make an Iced Latte at Home: Espresso, Milk and Ice
seo.description: Make a refreshing iced latte with 2 oz espresso, 6 oz cold milk and 1 cup of ice, plus no-machine methods using a moka pot or AeroPress.
